correctness.rationale: The 21 literal rows over \(\mathbb Z[a]/(a^2+a+2)\) are completely enumerated. Exact projective pair-equality yields 49 classes: 21 of multiplicity four and 28 of multiplicity three. The entire 1330 triple-determinant norm histogram has only zero or powers of two, proving incidence persistence for every prime away from two. At the two split primes, all 21 coefficient reductions and all 49 projective cross-vector valuations are computed by exact division by the respective norm-two uniformizers, giving the two Cartier equations and all stated collision counts. Reduced six/seven-line configurations give Tjurina 19/28 via the local ideals \((u^2,v^2)\) and (u,v). The Python verifier was run from the supplied actual package source and prints VERIFY_OK; limitations on unions of sections are explicit.

originality.rationale: The 2014 published Klein coefficient model and the generic 49-point structure are not novel and are explicitly credited. The assessed claim is the complete pair of distinct characteristic-two Cartier special fibres, exact two-prime specializations of every one of the 49 historically motivated intersection centres, and the determinant-norm certificate excluding other incidence-bad primes. Direct source comparison found no stated full collision profile; mathematical-record searches for aliases and positive-characteristic reductions did not return a comparable theorem. This is qualified priority because the published line equations make the reduction derivable and unindexed prior computations may exist.

value.rationale: The 49 Klein intersection points are natural centres in classical blowups. Their two inequivalent local specializations at rational primes above 2 create a marked geometric degeneration with 28-to-1 versus three 14-to-1 collisions, not inferred from the generic incidence diagram, and different Cartier multiplicities and reduced singularity invariants. The determinant norm histogram isolates the exact bad rational characteristic for this integral model. The theorem carefully avoids claiming a scheme-theoretic flat Hilbert limit or birational invariance.
